title: Watching a terminal, and bringing one forward
description: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/screen and POST /v1/sessions/{id}/focus. Reading a screen is the subscription: there is no route that attaches a pipe and none that takes one off, so a watcher that stops asking stops being a watcher and the machine state it created goes with it.

ScreenChannel.description: How a watcher finds out that a screen changed, which is a fact about the backend and not about the watcher. `signalled` is tmux with a pipe on the pane, about four milliseconds behind it; `on-demand` is a sample taken when somebody asks, no faster than `askAgainAfterMs`. Drawing the two identically would be a lie the reader has no way to catch, so it is in every payload.

PromptSuggestion.description: An unaccepted native Claude terminal suggestion, kept outside the draft. It is absent when styling, execution identity or the screen lease cannot prove it. This is terminal evidence, not an independently generated prediction.

observed_at.description: Monotonic Unix milliseconds when the native suggestion changed, for ordering snapshots and invalidations. Zero advertises support before the first watched capture.

Screen.description: One reading of a terminal. `backend` and `channel` come first because a screen with no backend named is the defect this exists to avoid, and `lines` is what came back rather than what was asked for: an alternate-screen program has no history to give and this must not imply otherwise.

revision.description: What a client compares to decide whether it already has this screen. FNV-1a over the UTF-8 bytes, which is enough for "did these change" and is deliberately not a promise about anything else. An unreadable screen is the constant `unreadable`, so a pane that stays unreadable stops producing events after the first one.

pending.description: Nothing has been captured for this session yet. The first read of a session answers this and the screen arrives a few milliseconds later on the `screen` event, because the answer comes out of a published snapshot and the capture happens behind it.

watchingUntil.description: Unix seconds. The lease this read renewed; a lease nobody renews expires and takes the pipe with it.

text.description: The capture, escape sequences kept. Absent until the first one completes.

lines.description: How many rows actually came back. The trailing newline a capture ends with is a terminator, not a row.

at.description: Unix seconds of the capture this text came from.

askAgainAfterMs.description: On `on-demand` only, said out loud rather than left for the client to discover: nothing will tell it the screen moved, so asking again is the only way to see a change, and this is the fastest it may.

ScreenEvent.description: The `screen` frame on /v1/events: only that a screen moved, and to what revision. The screen itself is fetched through the authenticated GET, exactly as a transcript append is — a stream frame reaches every device on this connection, and a terminal somebody else is watching has no business on it.

FocusResult.description: The session's terminal was asked to come forward. It says the selection was made on this machine, never that a window is now in front of a person: under tmux the emulator drawing the pane decides that, and the one that can be asked — iTerm2, whether it is mirroring the pane under `tmux -CC` or holding the pty an ordinary `tmux attach` is running in — is asked separately, after this answer has already gone out. What it does say is that somebody could see it: a tmux session with no client attached is refused as `nobody_attached` rather than answered `ok`.
